about: The Agimus tibi gratias is a short thanksgiving traditionally said after a meal. Those gathered thank almighty God for all his benefits and confess that he lives and reigns for ever.

s01.translation: We give you thanks, almighty God,

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)
Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

s03.translation: who live and reign for ever and ever. Amen.

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

w001.function: With “grátias”, it forms the fixed expression “grátias ágere” — to give thanks. Its ending expresses the first-person plural.

w002.function: The dative identifies God as the personal recipient of thanksgiving.

w003.function: The accusative plural is the object of “Ágimus” in the idiom meaning to give thanks.

w004.function: The vocative adjective agrees with “Deus” and names the addressee's almighty power.

w005.function: Here “Deus” is vocative: it identifies the addressee already indicated by “tibi”.

w006.function: The preposition with the ablative introduces the benefits for which thanks are given.

w007.function: The adjective includes the complete range of benefits, not only the gift of the meal.

w008.function: The ablative governed by “pro” names God's benefits as the reason for thanksgiving.

w009.function: The possessive relates the benefits to the God whom the faithful address.

w010.function: The relative is a nominative subject and resumes the God named by “Deus”. Its second-person verbs continue the direct address to God.

w011.function: The present second person predicates life of the God who remains directly addressed.

w012.function: The conjunction coordinates two predicates of the same addressee.

w013.function: The present second person confesses God's continuing reign.

w014.function: The preposition with the accusative introduces the fixed formula of unbounded duration.

w015.function: The accusative plural is governed by “in”.

w016.function: The genitive plural completes the idiom “ages of ages”, expressing eternity.

w017.function: The final assent embraces the whole thanksgiving and confession.
